name: Make a sine sub audible on phones and laptops: keep the 20-60 Hz fundamental but add pleasing harmonics in the 60-200 Hz bass range with volume-compensated hard clipping (odd harmonics) and/or an added overtone series (octave, fifth, octave), then scoop the honky low mids, low-pass the fizz, optionally add soft sine layers two and four octaves up, and tilt toward the top only if notes are still unclear
goal: Turn a pure sine/triangle sub into a bass line whose notes can be heard on small speakers without the listener noticing the distortion. Sub (20-60 Hz) is felt, not heard; consumer speakers reproduce 60-200 Hz, so the recipe adds controlled harmonics there and then cleans up their tone. Portable as a chain of generic processors (clipper, harmonic/octave layers, EQ scoop, low-pass, fast compressor, tilt EQ).

source.title: Create "Audible" Sub Bass in Ableton Live

prerequisites: A sine or triangle sub bass track
Hard clipper or saturator with output gain compensation, EQ with a bell cut and low-pass, a fast (multiband) compressor and a tilt EQ, or a synth that can add octave/fifth sine layers

inputs.name: sub_track
inputs.description: Sine/triangle sub line whose notes disappear on small speakers

outputs.name: audible_sub
outputs.description: Sub bass with harmonics in 60-200 Hz that translates to phones

outputs.name: processing_chain
outputs.description: Clip/harmonics → scoop → low-pass (→ fast comp → tilt) chain

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Keep the effect transparent: the goal is that the listener cannot tell the sine was distorted.
Real sub is only about one octave of notes (roughly 30-60 Hz); most speakers make little below 30 Hz, so judge on small speakers as well as monitors.
Steady pitch (Matt's taste): harmonics are fixed intervals (octaves, fifth); no pitch modulation, detune or wobble.
Original processing chain; the free device in the source is not required or copied.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only pad before that.

Polyrhythm Studio / Web Audio mapping: OscillatorNode + GainNode per layer, BiquadFilterNode (lowpass/highpass/allpass) for filters, DelayNode/ConvolverNode for space, AudioParam automation or slow custom LFOs for movement.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Check the sine sub on an analyzer: only the fundamental shows, inside 20-60 Hz, and the notes are hard to make out on small speakers.
Add volume-compensated hard clipping and raise it slowly until the bass line becomes audible. It adds odd harmonics (e.g. one at 139 Hz for a low F sharp).
steps.expect: Notes become readable; level stays the same

steps.action: Alternatively or in addition, add the harmonic overtone series to the sine: an octave, a fifth above that, and the next octave, at low levels.
steps.expect: A warmer, more musical set of audible harmonics

steps.action: Scoop the low mid-range that the harmonics create with a bell cut, which also emphasizes the lows and makes the bass less honky.
Low-pass the result to tame the upper harmonics and any fizz.
steps.expect: Clean, round tone that still reads on phones

steps.action: To keep a subby, 'wumpy' character instead of grit, add soft triangle/sine-like layers two octaves up and four octaves up and set their level with the low-pass. A little saturation on top goes a long way.
steps.expect: Subby tone with audible upper octaves

steps.action: For a thinner, different distortion color, compress the sub with a very fast attack and fast release (multiband if available); low-pass afterwards to clean up the aliasing junk.
steps.expect: Extra odd harmonics with a thinner tone

steps.action: If notes are still unclear, tilt the EQ to favor the top and reduce the sub, re-scoop a little and low-pass again. Check on phone/laptop speakers and on headphones.
steps.expect: Bass line clearly audible across playback systems

verification: On a spectrum analyzer the bass now has clear energy between 60 and 200 Hz, not only below 60 Hz.
Bass notes can be identified on a phone or laptop speaker.
The level matches the dry sub (gain-compensated) when A/B'd.
No audible fizz or aliasing above the low-pass.
